podcast.title: Political Activism and Censorship (1967-1969)
podcast.body: Initially appearing as innocuous "young white young men" in matching blazers, the Smothers Brothers quickly became television renegades on their CBS show. They grew increasingly political and critical of the Johnson administration and featured rock and roll bands to connect with a younger audience. Their material, especially its anti-Vietnam War stance, led to frequent censorship of segments and even entire episodes, ultimately resulting in the show's abrupt cancellation in April 1969 after two years. "It did not take long though before the Smothers Brothers began to get very political and critical of the Johnson administration."

podcast.title: Smothers Brothers Summer Show (1968)
podcast.body: In 1968, Tommy and Dick Smothers produced a summer show during the traditional network TV break. This program was hosted by Glenn Campbell and performed well enough to lead to Campbell's own variety series as a replacement for the canceled Smothers Brothers Show. "In 1968, Tommy and Dick Smothers produced the Smothers Brothers Summer Show. The host of their summer show was Glenn Campbell."

podcast.title: Steve Martin as Writer
podcast.body: Steve Martin was a writer for The Smothers Brothers Show, contributing to the comedic and often politically charged material that defined the program. "by the way, Steve Martin was a writer on that show."
